POKOMO & BAJUNI CULTURAL HERITAGE

The living heritage of Kenya’s coast, kept for the next generation.

Discover the traditions, languages, stories and artifacts of the Pokomo and Bajuni peoples — digitised in 3D, recorded from elders and curated with the National Museums of Kenya.

WHY THIS ARCHIVE EXISTS

Preserving memory before it fades

Indigenous dialects, oral poetry and the craft knowledge of coastal families are passed down by voice and by hand. This platform records them with communities — so they can be seen, heard and learned anywhere.

Our mission

To preserve, revitalise and promote the cultural heritage of the Pokomo and Bajuni communities through AI, digital archives and community-driven storytelling.

Our vision

A future where the languages, oral histories, artifacts and traditions of coastal Kenya are digitally preserved, widely accessible and celebrated by future generations.

TWO COMMUNITIES, ONE COAST

Kenya’s coastal peoples

The histories, environments and languages of the peoples shaping this archive.

MARITIME CIVILISATION · LAMU ARCHIPELAGO

The Bajuni

Language: Kibajuni

One of the oldest coastal communities of the northern Kenyan coast and the Lamu islands, with an identity bound to the Indian Ocean — renowned for seafaring, dugout-canoe fishing and dhow building, and a blend of African, Arab and Swahili civilisations. Kibajuni carries rich maritime vocabulary and proverbs of unity, courage and respect for the sea.

Explore Bajuni artifacts

RIVERINE CUSTODIANS · TANA RIVER BASIN

The Pokomo

Language: Kipokomo

Farmers and river custodians of the lower Tana floodplains, with deep ecological knowledge and basket-fishing techniques passed down the generations. Life is organised around extended families and elders, guided by consensus. Kipokomo holds river folktales that teach patience, cooperation and respect for nature.

Explore Pokomo artifacts

ORAL TRADITIONS

Stories, songs & poetry
Traditional legends, Tana River flood songs, monsoon sailing melodies and Bajuni mashairi — recorded with the people who carry them.

FEATURED COLLECTION

Mashairi ya Mohamed Kombo

Mohamed Kombo is one of the foremost Bajuni poets. In his mashairi he tells the history of his people and reflects on life and human relationships, with a mastery of Bajuni figurative language widely respected in his community.

Recordings courtesy of Bajuni Cultural Heritage · curated by Gideon Ngaruiya

Listen

Recordings are being digitised

The first poems and stories are being prepared for publication. Elders and community members can contribute a recording.

GET INVOLVED

Become a digital heritage custodian
Help document rare artifacts, oral stories, coastal songs and languages from your elders.

COLLECTIVE ARCHIVING

Save our heritage together

This platform belongs to the communities it preserves. True preservation is community-driven: we work with families, youth, fishermen, farmers and elders in Lamu, Tana River and Mombasa, gathering memories and records directly from their sources.

Apply below to join as a contributor. Once approved you get access to the Studio, where you can create records, upload photographs, 3D scans and recordings of any size, and follow each submission through curator review.

Community workshops

Regular workshops in Lamu and Tana River counties teach how to record high-fidelity interviews and take archive-quality photographs.

Have heirlooms at home?

Our team can create 3D digital reconstructions of family objects so they survive for future generations.

Already a contributor?

Sign in to the Studio to upload files and track approvals.
